t.1.51.1: On seeing Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of those who murmur prayers, the mighty hero Viśvāmitra was supremely delighted and bowed low out of humility.
t.1.51.2: He was told by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, "Welcome to you," and the blessed Vasiṣṭha had a seat offered to him.
t.1.51.3: And then, when the wise Viśvāmitra had taken his seat, the best of sages offered him fruits and roots in due accordance with custom.
t.1.51.4: Having accepted that worship from Vasiṣṭha, the best of kings inquired after the welfare of his austerities, his agnihotra fire-rites, and his disciples.
t.1.51.6: When King Viśvāmitra was comfortably seated, Vasiṣṭha of great austerity, the son of Brahmā and foremost among those who murmur prayers, questioned him.
t.1.51.5: Viśvāmitra of great splendor likewise asked after the welfare of the groves of trees, and Vasiṣṭha told that best of kings that all was well everywhere.
t.1.51.7: Is all well with you, O king? O righteous one, do you protect your subjects, O king, delighting them through dharma and through the conduct befitting a king?
t.1.51.8: Are your servants well provided for? Do they abide by your command? Have all your enemies been conquered, O slayer of foes?
t.1.51.9: O scorcher of foes, is all well with you in your army, your treasury and your allies, O tiger among men, and likewise with your sons and grandsons, O sinless one?
t.1.51.10: The king, the mighty and radiant Viśvāmitra, full of humility, replied to Vasiṣṭha that all was well in every respect.
t.1.51.11: Having carried on those auspicious conversations for a long time, the two most righteous ones, filled with supreme joy, delighted in each other.
t.1.51.12: Then, O Raghunandana, at the end of their conversation, the blessed Vasiṣṭha, as if smiling, spoke these words to Viśvāmitra.
t.1.51.14: May your honour accept this hospitality offered by me. O king, you are the foremost of guests and must be honoured with every effort.
t.1.51.13: O mighty one, I wish to offer hospitality to this army and to you, whose greatness is beyond measure; accept it from me as is fitting.
t.1.51.15: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, the greatly wise King Viśvāmitra said, "By your words of honour, all has been done for me by you."
t.1.51.17: O greatly wise one, I have been well honored in every way by you who are worthy of honor. I shall depart; salutations to you, look upon me with a friendly eye.
t.1.51.16: O blessed one, with the fruits and roots that are found in your hermitage, with water for washing the feet and water for sipping, and with the sight of your holy self, I have been honored.
t.1.51.18: As the king spoke thus, the righteous and noble-minded Vasiṣṭha invited him once more, again and again.
t.1.51.19: Gādheya replied to Vasiṣṭha, "Very well! Let it be as is pleasing to the revered one, O best of sages."
t.1.51.20: Thus addressed, the greatly radiant Vasiṣṭha, foremost among those who murmur prayers, he whose sins had been washed away, was pleased and then called forth the spotted cow.
t.1.51.21: Come, come quickly, Śabalā, and listen to my words: I have resolved to entertain this royal sage together with his army. Arrange for me a reception for him with food of great value.
t.1.51.23: Hurry, O Śabalā, and bring forth a whole abundance of foods, furnished with savory dishes, with cooked grain and drinks, and with things to be licked and to be sucked.
t.1.51.22: Whatever each one desires, as he wishes, that is prized among the six flavours, all of that, O divine wish-yielding cow, you who shower down abundance, rain forth for my sake.
